title: Unformatted I/O — binary write with vendor-specific record markers (4-byte length prefix on most Unix)
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE DUMP_BLOCK(UNIT, A)
C     WRITE without FORMAT writes binary. Most Unix Fortran
C     compilers prefix each unformatted record with a 4-byte length
C     marker AND append the same length at the end. A direct Java
C     port that just writes 320 bytes of REAL*4 produces a file the
C     legacy reader (which expects the markers) cannot parse.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER UNIT
      REAL    A(80)
      WRITE (UNIT) A
C     ^ writes [4-byte len][320 bytes data][4-byte len]
      END
notes: Unformatted sequential I/O has implementation-defined record markers. Migrating only the writer (or only the reader) means the two halves can no longer talk. The spec must surface this so the SME decides: migrate both endpoints in lockstep, or add a marker-aware adapter.
